tasks.summary: The reconciliation touches only the ISSUE artifact, its docs, and the test fixture (src/daemon/db/__tests__/fixtures/session-source-inventory.json); no production or scanner source was modified, matching the fix intent. Cross-checking the fixture diff against the ISSUE/t13-sweep claims confirms: 57 new classification entries added (matches "57 unlisted production files"), 0 removed classification lines (matches "no removed entries"), ~38 rationale changes and ~119 sourceDigest changes among pre-existing entries (closely matches the follow-up note's 37 site-changed / 81 source-only-changed split), the sc6Sources removal-source set still lists exactly the 17 files the gate test expects with rationale length well over the 80-char floor and the method-class.ts rationale still matches /affinity remains release-blocking/, and the connection-management-gates.json readiness gate (ready:false, scopes:[]) was left untouched by this commit and is still asserted disabled by both CM-S3-INVENTORY and CM-S4-GATE. The t13-backend-sweep.md follow-up's "passed all 12 tests" claim matches the actual case count across the four named test files (3+5+2+2=12).

testCoverage.explanation: The four named test files are the right coverage for this change: session-source-inventory.test.ts's CM-S3-INVENTORY and CM-S4-GATE tests assert directly against the reconciled fixture (file/site/digest parity with the actual scanned source, plus the sc6Sources removal-source set and the disabled-gate invariant), and connection-execution.test.ts / connection-consumers.test.ts / composed-probe-logs.test.ts are the 'connection privacy regressions' the fix intent calls for alongside the inventory check. I verified the test bodies assert what the builder claims (gate.ready===false, gate.scopes excludes/equals empty, sc6Sources key set and rationale-length/digest checks, per-file site/digest/classification parity) rather than taking the pass report at face value, and cross-checked the builder's '12 tests' claim by counting test() cases in the four files (3+5+2+2=12), which matches exactly.

advice: Optional execution: I did not run the test suite, tsc, or compute file digests myself in this review session — the sandbox's command-approval gate blocked `node`, `shasum`, and even `grep -c`/`wc -l` pipelines beyond a few permitted git-show/grep forms, so I could not execute `node --import tsx --test ... session-source-inventory.test.ts ...` or `tsc --noEmit` to directly reproduce the builder's reported pass. I instead cross-checked the claimed figures (57 new files, 0 removed, 37/81 site/source split, 12 passing tests) against the actual git diff and test bodies using the git-show/grep commands that were permitted, and every figure matched or was within expected rounding of the fixture diff.

Optional improvement: several of the 57 newly-classified fixture entries share a verbatim boundary-doctrine sentence (e.g. the 'Persistent workflow/document-generation/knowledge-service execution is outside supported session methods...' and 'Analysis may consume temporary sources...' openers) across many distinct files, with only a short file-specific second sentence appended. This mirrors the existing style already present in the pre-change fixture (and is consistent with the pattern used for the mechanically-reclassified entries, which honestly self-label as 'not an independent review'), so it is not a regression, but a future audit pass could foreground the file-specific clause first for scanability.

cases: CM-S3-INVENTORY: production boundaries have explicit reviewed classifications and unchanged baseline
CM-S3-INVENTORY: renamed and destructured provider resolver factory serializer and filesystem APIs are discovered
CM-S4-GATE: reviewed removal sources include pure helpers owner boundaries and pending global affinity
